CHAPTER ONE: INTRODUCTION
1.1 Background of SIWES
SIWES was established by the Industrial Training Fund (ITF) in 1973 to address the shortage of practical skills among Nigerian graduates. It is a tripartite arrangement between students, institutions and industry.
1.2 Objectives of SIWES
i. To expose students to industrial work experience
ii. To bridge the gap between theory and practice
iii. To prepare students for the work environment after graduation
iv. To make the transition from school to the world of work easier
v. To enhance students contacts with potential employers
vi. To provide an avenue for students to acquire industrial skills
1.3 Importance of SIWES
SIWES helps students apply classroom knowledge to real-world situations.
1.4 Scope of the Training
Training took place at the ICT Centre, Lagos State University of Science and Technology, University Campus, Ikorodu, Lagos. I was posted to the hardware maintenance unit where I worked on computer assembly and network troubleshooting.
1.5 Duration of the Training
The training lasted from 2 March 2026 to 22 May 2026.

CHAPTER TWO: BRIEF HISTORY AND ORGANISATIONAL STRUCTURE
2.1 Brief History of the Organisation
The ICT Centre was established to support ICT training and services for the university community.
2.2 Objectives of the Organisation
To provide ICT infrastructure and training support to students and staff.
2.3 Organisational Structure
The Centre is led by a Director who oversees technical and administrative units.
2.4 Organogram of the Organisation
Director
  Technical Unit
    Hardware Maintenance
    Network Administration
  Administrative Unit
    Finance
    Records

CHAPTER THREE: ACTIVITIES AND EXPERIENCE DURING SIWES
3.1 Duties and Responsibilities
I identified computer components and assisted with hardware assembly.
3.2 Activities Performed
WEEK 1-2: Component Identification
I identified motherboard, CPU, RAM, and storage components. I learned to distinguish between different form factors and specifications.
WEEK 3-5: Assembly and RAM Installation
I assembled desktop computers and installed RAM modules. I verified each installation by booting the system and checking BIOS detection.
WEEK 6-8: Troubleshooting and OS Installation
I diagnosed faulty computers and installed operating systems. I used bootable USB drives to deploy Windows and Linux.
WEEK 9-12: Cyber Security
I configured firewalls and performed vulnerability scans. I documented security findings for the Centre's records.
3.3 Skills Acquired
Hardware assembly, operating system installation, network troubleshooting.
3.4 Equipment/Tools Used
Screwdriver set, multimeter, crimping tool, bootable USB drive.
3.5 Challenges Encountered
1. Some computers had corrupted BIOS settings.
3.6 Solutions to the Challenges
1. I reset the BIOS to factory defaults and reconfigured boot priority.

CHAPTER FOUR: SUMMARY, CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATIONS
4.1 Summary
During twelve weeks at the ICT Centre, I assembled computers, installed operating systems, and performed network troubleshooting.
4.2 Conclusion
The training gave me practical experience in hardware maintenance and cyber security fundamentals.
4.3 Recommendations
1. ITF should increase stipend funding for trainees.
2. NUC should require all universities to maintain functional ICT centres.
3. The university should extend the SIWES duration to six months.
